_status: General guidance. To be verified with the architecture firm.

stone.durability: Very durable; lasts decades. Softer stones (marble, limestone) scratch and etch with acids.
stone.water: Porous; needs sealing, especially in wet areas.
stone.maintenance: Seal every 1-2 years; wipe spills quickly; avoid acidic cleaners on marble.
stone.install: Laid on cement-based stone adhesive or mortar bed; polished after laying for floors.

countertop.durability: Hard-wearing work surfaces; quartz and sintered stone resist stains and scratches well.
countertop.water: Engineered surfaces are non-porous; natural stone needs sealing.
countertop.maintenance: Mild soap and water; use trivets for very hot pans on quartz.
countertop.install: Templated on site, cut to size, fixed on the cabinet carcass with silicone / epoxy; edges profiled.
cons: quartz can mark with direct high heat

tile.durability: Very durable; vitrified and porcelain tiles resist scratches and stains.
tile.water: Low water absorption; good for wet areas (use anti-skid on wet floors).
tile.maintenance: Easy: mop and mild cleaner; re-grout or seal grout lines over time.
tile.install: Laid with tile adhesive on a level base, joints filled with grout; large formats need levelling clips.
pros: huge range of looks (stone, wood, concrete)

wood_floor.durability: Good for homes; engineered wood can be re-sanded once or twice; laminate and SPC resist scratches.
wood_floor.water: Avoid standing water; SPC / vinyl is waterproof, laminate and wood are not.
wood_floor.maintenance: Dry mop or damp cloth; felt pads under furniture; re-oil or re-coat wood over years.
wood_floor.install: Floating click system over underlay, or glued down; leave expansion gaps at the walls.

wood_panel.durability: Durable indoors when finished (PU / melamine); edges can chip if knocked.
wood_panel.water: Not for wet areas; keep away from direct water.
wood_panel.maintenance: Dust and wipe with a dry cloth; touch up polish on veneer when needed.
wood_panel.install: Fixed on a plywood or MDF backing (or a batten frame) with adhesive and pins; veneer is polished on site.

paint.durability: Lasts 5-8 years indoors before a repaint; washable emulsions clean better.
paint.water: Washable or moisture-resistant grades needed for kitchens and bathrooms.
paint.maintenance: Wipe with a damp cloth (washable grades); touch up as needed.
paint.install: Wall putty (2 coats) and primer first, then 2 coats of paint.
cons: marks and scuffs on busy walls
avoid: behind the hob or sink (use tile or glass)

plaster.durability: Durable seamless finish; can hairline-crack if the base moves.
plaster.water: Microcement / tadelakt can be sealed for wet areas; lime plaster prefers dry walls.
plaster.maintenance: Wipe gently; re-seal sealed finishes every few years.
plaster.install: Applied by skilled applicators in thin coats on a primed base, then sealed.

wallcovering.durability: Good for 7-10 years in dry rooms; vinyl types are scrubbable.
wallcovering.maintenance: Dust or wipe gently (vinyl: damp cloth).
wallcovering.install: Pasted on a smooth, primed wall; patterns need matching (more wastage).
pros: patterns and textures paint cannot do

cladding.durability: Very durable; brick and stone cladding last decades.
cladding.water: Seal brick / stone if exposed to rain.
cladding.maintenance: Brush clean; reseal every few years outdoors.
cladding.install: Fixed with adhesive on a rough-plastered wall; joints pointed.

ceiling.durability: Long life indoors; gypsum boards can sag or stain if water leaks above.
ceiling.water: Use moisture-resistant boards in bathrooms and kitchens.
ceiling.maintenance: Repaint every few years; fix leaks above quickly.
ceiling.install: Metal framing hung from the slab, boards screwed on, joints taped, puttied and painted.

cabinet.durability: Depends on the shutter finish; acrylic and PU are tougher on the surface, laminate on wear.
cabinet.water: Use BWP (boiling water proof) ply for sink cabinets.
cabinet.maintenance: Wipe with a soft damp cloth; avoid abrasive cleaners on gloss.
cabinet.install: Carcass built in ply, shutters fixed with soft-close hinges; edges banded.

facade.durability: Built for weather; check UV and fire ratings.
facade.water: Weatherproof by design; joints must be sealed.
facade.install: Fixed on a sub-frame anchored to the structure.
cons: fire rating matters for tall buildings

glass.durability: Toughened glass is strong; scratches show on mirrors and lacquered glass.
glass.water: Waterproof; great for backsplashes and shower areas.
glass.install: Cut to size and fixed with structural silicone or clips; toughened glass cannot be cut on site.
avoid: areas where it can be hit hard (unless toughened)

italian_marble.durability: Hard but softer than granite; etches with lemon, vinegar and some cleaners.

granite.durability: One of the hardest natural stones; very resistant to heat and scratches.

quartz.durability: Very hard, non-porous engineered stone; resists stains; can discolour with direct high heat or sun.

sintered_stone.durability: Extremely hard and heat resistant; very thin slabs need careful handling.

solid_surface.durability: Softer; scratches can be sanded out; seamless joints and integrated sinks.

laminate_panel.durability: Tough, scratch-resistant surface; edges are the weak point.

wpc_louvers.water: WPC is moisture resistant; suits semi-wet and covered outdoor spots.

spc_vinyl.water: Waterproof core; fine for kitchens and bathrooms (not showers).

room_needs._help: What a room needs from its finishes. wet: water-resistant; outdoor: weather-resistant; heat: near a hob; traffic: heavy foot traffic.
